source: Adapted from the school Drive Quran folder (TPS Quran Tracker: tajweed rules by year, Years 1-6 progression); Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf (Hafs 'an 'Asim)

lessons.title: Heavy and light letters
objectives: Name the seven heavy letters
Say heavy letters with a full mouth
Say light letters with a thin sound

keywords.def: raising the back of the tongue towards the roof of the mouth

starter: Bismillah. Name the five qalqalah letters.
Which rule hides the noon before the 15 letters?
Recite Al-Fil ayah 1 from the mushaf.

teach.heading: Two kinds of letters
bullets: Some letters are heavy, some are light
teach.note: Contrast the sound of a heavy ص with a light س. Ask the class to feel the back of the tongue rise for the heavy letter. Explain that heavy and light changes the letter, so it matters for meaning.

teach.heading: The seven heavy letters
bullets: خ  ص  ض  غ  ط  ق  ظ
The tongue rises to the roof of the mouth
teach.note: Teach the phrase خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ and the seven letters. Chant it three times. Say that these seven letters are always heavy, whatever vowel they carry.

teach.heading: Heavy in words
teach.note: Use examples from Al-Ikhlas and Al-Fatihah. The vowel after a heavy letter also sounds fuller. Misconception: only the letter is heavy; the fathah after it should also sound full.

teach.heading: Light in words
teach.note: Compare pairs: سَ / صَ, تِ / طِ, كُ / قُ. Light letters keep the tongue low. Children echo each pair and say heavy or light.

teach.heading: Why it matters
bullets: A wrong sound can change the word
teach.note: This is a real example of how a light kaaf in place of a heavy qaaf changes the word. Do not stress fear: stress care and love for the words of Allah.

practice: Is the first letter of الصَّمَدُ heavy or light?
independent: Sort 12 letters into heavy or light
Read 8 word pairs aloud (سَ/صَ, تِ/طِ, كُ/قُ)
Find three heavy letters in Al-Ikhlas and read them
exit: Why does a heavy letter matter?
lessons.homework: Chant the seven heavy letters daily and read Al-Ikhlas with a full mouth on ق ص.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: mirror work - tongue low (light) and raised (heavy). Stretch: find heavy letters in Al-Falaq.

lessons.title: Temporary heavy letters: raa and laam in Allah
objectives: Know that raa and the laam of Allah can be heavy or light
Apply the vowel rule for raa
Apply the vowel rule for the laam of Allah

keywords.def: the letter ر: heavy or light by its vowel
the laam in the name اللَّه

starter: Why is a heavy letter important?

teach.heading: Not always heavy
bullets: Raa and the laam of Allah are sometimes heavy, sometimes light
teach.note: Explain that unlike the seven, these two change. Ask: which letters are always heavy? Which can change? Use the word 'temporary'.

teach.heading: Raa with a vowel
bullets: Raa with fathah or dammah: heavy
teach.note: Cite رَبِّ النَّاسِ (An-Nas) and رِحْلَةَ (Quraysh 106:2). Children hear the fuller raa in رَبِّ and the thin raa in رِحْلَةَ. Check: say the vowel first, then the sound.

teach.heading: Laam of Allah
teach.note: Use Al-Ikhlas هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (after damma: heavy) and the bismillah (after kasra: light). Ask: what comes before the laam? Link the vowel to the sound.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: Say the vowel before the laam
teach.note: Do a call-and-response drill with fast examples: رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (heavy), لِلَّهِ (light). Keep it light-hearted. Every child says it aloud.

practice: Is the raa in رِحْلَةَ heavy or light?
Is the laam in بِسْمِ اللَّهِ heavy or light?
independent: Read 8 words with raa and decide heavy or light
Mark the laam of Allah in Al-Ikhlas and the bismillah
Pairs: test each other on the vowel rule
exit: What decides if raa is heavy or light?
Give an example of a light laam in Allah.
lessons.homework: Read the bismillah and Al-Ikhlas ayah 1 daily, noticing the laam of Allah.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour kasrah in blue (light) and fathah/dammah in red (heavy). Stretch: find raa words in Al-Fatihah and label them.

lessons.title: Major mistakes: errors in letters and vowels
objectives: Know what a major mistake is
Find common letter mix-ups
Self-correct while reading

keywords.def: an error that changes a letter or a vowel and so may change the meaning

starter: Is the raa in رَبِّ heavy or light?

teach.heading: Two kinds of mistakes
bullets: Major mistakes change a letter or vowel
Minor mistakes miss a rule of beauty
teach.note: Explain gently: all of us make mistakes when learning. The aim is to notice and fix. Remind pupils of the hadith narrated by Aisha (RA) in Bukhari and Muslim: the one who recites the Qur'an skilfully is with the noble angels, and the one who finds it hard and persists has a double reward. Keep the tone encouraging.

teach.heading: Common letter mix-ups
teach.note: Say each pair. Show how the mix-up changes a word, for example قُلْ and كُلْ. Children try each pair and listen to a partner. Ask: how can we tell?

teach.heading: Vowel mix-ups
bullets: Short vowels made long, or long made short
teach.note: Fatihah 1:7: أَنْعَمْتَ means 'You (Allah) favoured'; with a dammah, أَنْعَمْتُ would mean 'I favoured', which is a wrong meaning. Teach positively: vowels carry meaning.

teach.heading: How to fix it
teach.note: Offer a simple routine: slow, isolate the letter, repeat. Praise anyone who spots and corrects their own error. Encourage listening to a recording by a good reciter.

practice: Name a pair of letters that are easy to mix up.
Why does قُلْ differ from كُلْ?
independent: Teacher reads with deliberate errors; children raise a hand
Read Al-Fil ayat 1-3 slowly and self-check
Practise the four mix-up pairs with word cards
exit: Give one way to fix a mistake.
lessons.homework: Read Al-Fil ayat 1-3 to a family member and ask them to listen for any letter that is unclear.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio of the correct sound and picture of mouth position. Stretch: write a short note on why accuracy is a sign of respect.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: At-Tin and the noon sakinah rules
lessons.title: Idgham with ghunnah: merging the noon into ي ن م و
lessons.bigQuestion: When two friends hold hands and walk as one, are they still two people? What happens to a noon when it 'holds hands' with the next letter?
objectives: To understand how noon sakinah and tanween merge with a humming sound into the letters of يَنْمُو
successCriteria: All: name the four letters of idgham with ghunnah
Most: read idgham with a two-count hum
Some: explain why the noon is not written with a sukoon there
lessons.smsc: Social: we merge together kindly in our class like the letters, listening and taking turns

keywords.def: merging the noon into the next letter
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon
the four letters of idgham with ghunnah: ي ن م و

hook.text: When two friends hold hands and walk as one, are they still two people? What happens to a noon when it 'holds hands' with the next letter?
hook.a: The noon joins into the next letter and disappears into it, but leaves a two-count hum: idgham with ghunnah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance' (Al-Qamar 54:17). Rules like idgham make the recitation flow smoothly.

starter.q: Izhar happens before ...
Al-Qadr 97:5: «سَلَٰمٌ هِىَ ...» Which word comes next?
Which word is izhar?

teach.heading: Idgham: merging
bullets: Idgham letters: ي ر م ل و ن
Two kinds: with and without ghunnah
teach.note: Bismillah. Idgham means to merge one letter into the next. It only happens across two words (except a few words we learn later).

teach.heading: With ghunnah: يَنْمُو
teach.note: Four letters: ي ن م و. The noon disappears into the letter and we hum for two counts.

teach.heading: How do I know? Look at the mushaf
bullets: Tanween written one above the other, slanted
teach.note: Show مِّن مَّسَدٍ in the mushaf: no sukoon on the noon, a shaddah on the meem. The mushaf shows us the rule.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: two-count hum
teach.note: Show two fingers for the two counts. Pupils unmute in turn and repeat each example.
cycle: Class shows two fingers for the hum

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: «مِّن مَّسَدٍ»: the noon meets meem (م). How do we read it?
options: Merge into the meem with a two-count hum
check.why: Meem is one of يَنْمُو, so it is idgham with ghunnah. Clear noon is for throat letters; nothing changes into baa.

practice.q: Read «حَبْلٌ مِّن مَّسَدٍ» (111:5). How many idgham with ghunnah can you hear?
practice.a: Two: حَبْلٌۭ مِّن (tanween into meem) and مِّن مَّسَدٍ (noon into meem).
practice.model: I do: حَبْلٌ has tanween, next letter م: idgham with ghunnah. Then مِّن, next letter م again: idgham with ghunnah. I read: hablum-mim-masad, humming two counts twice.

practice.q: Which letter is NOT in يَنْمُو?
practice.a: ر

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, colour every idgham with ghunnah in Al-Bayyinah 98:2 and Al-Masad 111:1 and 5. Today's rota group reads 97:1 to 5 to the teacher in turn.
independent.model: The teacher colours the first one: رَسُولٌۭ مِّنَ in 98:2, tanween then meem, so idgham with ghunnah.

independent.q: Extend: write the word يَنْمُو and colour its four letters.
independent.a: ي ن م و

independent.q: Stretch: in 97:4 «رَبِّهِم مِّن», which letter is merging, noon or meem?
independent.a: Meem: a meem sakinah merges into the next meem with ghunnah (we learn meem rules in Spring 2).

exit.a: idgham with ghunnah

exit.q: Back to our ponder: When two friends hold hands and walk as one, are they still two people? What happens to a noon when it 'holds hands' with the next letter?
exit.a: The noon joins into the next letter and disappears into it, but leaves a two-count hum: idgham with ghunnah.

lessons.homework: Read Al-Masad 111:1 and 5 to a parent with the two-count hum; tick the revision log.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Idgham and the family of madd
lessons.title: Madd badal and madd 'iwad
objectives: Know madd badal (hamza before a madd letter)
Know madd 'iwad (stopping on tanween fathah)
Read each at two counts

keywords.def: a hamza followed by a madd letter: 2 counts
stopping on tanween -an turns it into a long 'aa': 2 counts

teach.heading: Madd badal
bullets: Hamza comes first, then the madd letter
teach.note: The madd letter replaces a second hamza (badal means substitute). Pupils tap two counts. Example: آمَنُوا from Al-Asr 103:3. Make the link: the letter is natural-length, not four counts.

teach.heading: Madd 'iwad
bullets: The tanween turns into a long alif
teach.note: Give examples from the surahs: أَفْوَاجًا in An-Nasr 110:2 and تَوَّابًا in 110:3. Pupils stop on the word and hear the long 'aa'. 'Iwad means compensation.

teach.heading: When it does not apply
bullets: If you continue, say tanween -an normally
Tanween on ة (round taa) does not make 'iwad
teach.note: Misconception: stretching tanween when continuing. Contrast reading on without stopping (tanween -an said as normal) with stopping (long aa). A round ة becomes a haa when stopping, not an alif.

teach.heading: Counting lengths
teach.note: Review the length ladder on the board. Ask: which are the shortest? Which longest? Children move hands low for two counts and high for six.

practice: Stop on أَفْوَاجًا. What do you say at the end?
independent: Find madd badal in Al-Asr and An-Nasr
Practise stopping on tanween fathah words
Sort 10 words into natural, badal, 'iwad, muttasil
lessons.homework: Recite An-Nasr daily, stopping at each ayah and noticing the madd 'iwad.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: hand-height madd gestures. Stretch: explain why badal means 'substitute'.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Idgham and the family of madd
lessons.title: Madd lazim: the six-count madd
objectives: Know madd lazim has six counts
Spot a shaddah or sukoon after a madd letter
Read الضَّالِّينَ correctly

keywords.def: a madd letter followed by a fixed sukoon or shaddah: 6 counts

teach.heading: Six counts
bullets: Madd letter + shaddah or fixed sukoon
teach.note: Show the length ladder again. Lazim means necessary: the length is fixed. Ask: why is the fixed sukoon or shaddah a reason to stretch longer? Accept ideas and keep it brief.

teach.heading: Example
bullets: Stretch six counts, then the shaddah
teach.note: Al-Fatihah ends with وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ: this is the most famous example. Model a steady six-count stretch. Ask: where is the alif and the shaddah?

teach.heading: Word and letter
bullets: Madd lazim kalimi: in a word
Madd lazim harfi: in the names of some letters
teach.note: Introduce briefly. The harfi type occurs in the opening letters of some surahs and will be met later. Year 3 focus: the kalimi type in الضَّالِّينَ.

teach.heading: Practise
teach.note: Pair work: one recites الضَّالِّينَ, the other counts on fingers. Correct both shortening and over-extending. Keep each pupil's confidence high.

practice: How many counts for madd lazim?
Find the madd lazim in Al-Fatihah ayah 7.
independent: Recite Al-Fatihah and mark the madd lazim
Read 6 words and decide: 2, 4 or 6 counts
Order the madd types by length
exit: What follows the madd letter in madd lazim?
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fatihah daily with a steady six-count madd on الضَّالِّينَ.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: finger counting to six and a length ladder poster. Stretch: explain lazim kalimi vs harfi in your own words.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surahs of the elephant and Quraysh
lessons.title: Surat Al-Fil
objectives: Recite Al-Fil accurately
Apply rules from the term
Learn the meaning

teach.heading: The surah
bullets: أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَابِ الْفِيلِ
teach.note: Tell briefly how Allah protected the Ka'bah from the people of the elephant in the year the Prophet ﷺ was born, as the scholars of seerah relate. Chunk and echo the first two ayat.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
teach.note: Meaning: He sent birds in flocks; they threw baked clay stones at them; and He made them like eaten straw. Practise slowly in chunks.

teach.heading: Rules in the surah
teach.note: Children find each rule in the mushaf and label it. Also point out مِن سِجِّيلٍ: the noon sakinah meets seen, so it is ikhfa. Ask pupils to say which of the noon rules each phrase uses.

teach.heading: Meaning and lesson
bullets: His power is above every army
teach.note: Draw out: Allah is in control. Ask: how does this help us when we feel small? Link to tawakkul.

practice: Find the rule in تَرْمِيهِم بِحِجَارَةٍ.
independent: Read Al-Fil in pairs, marking rules
Memorise ayat 1-2 using listen/read/cover
Individual recitation to teacher
exit: What does the surah teach us about Allah?
lessons.homework: Practise Al-Fil ayat 1-5 daily, learning ayat 1-3 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: echo-chunk with picture cues. Stretch: memorise the full surah.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Surahs of the elephant and Quraysh
lessons.title: Surat Quraysh
objectives: Recite Quraysh accurately
Apply madd and heavy-light rules
Reflect on gratitude for provision
starter: Is the raa in رِحْلَةَ heavy or light?

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Quraysh were traders who travelled in winter and in summer. Chunk and echo. Ask: why would a safe journey matter to traders?

teach.heading: Ayat 3-4
teach.note: Meaning: so let them worship the Lord of this House, who fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear. Two blessings: food and safety.

teach.heading: Rules in the surah
teach.note: Pupils label the rules. Madd muttasil in الشِّتَاءِ: four counts. Revise the tafkheem rule for raa from earlier in the term.

teach.heading: Gratitude
bullets: Food and safety come from Allah
teach.note: Ask: what are three blessings you had today? Link to shukr. Keep the discussion warm and brief.

independent: Read Quraysh in pairs; mark heavy and light raa
Memorise ayat 1-2, then 3-4
Recite Al-Fil and Quraysh back to back
exit: Which two blessings does Quraysh mention?
Give one rule from the surah.
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Fil and Quraysh daily and write three blessings you are thankful for.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and sentence frames for gratitude. Stretch: link the surah to your own day.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: At-Tin and the noon sakinah rules
lessons.title: Surat Al-Qadr 97:1-3: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Why might one special night be better than a thousand months?
objectives: To memorise Al-Qadr 97:1-3 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 97:1-3 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 97:1-3 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 97:1-3 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: wonder at the night the Qur'an was first sent down and the great reward Allah gives

keywords.def: the Decree: the name of the surah

hook.text: Why might one special night be better than a thousand months?
hook.a: Allah chose it: the Qur'an was first sent down on it, and good deeds on it are worth more than a thousand months (97:3).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, We sent it (the Qur'an) down during the Night of Decree' (Al-Qadr 97:1). The Qur'an came down in the month of Ramadan (Al-Baqarah 2:185). Learning this surah is learning about the night the Qur'an began.

starter.q: Which surah begins «قُلْ هُوَ ...»?
How many ayat are in Surat Al-'Asr (سورة العصر)?
Which word has tanween?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Qadr 97:1-3
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 97:1-3 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ فِى لَيْلَةِ ٱلْقَدْرِ (١) وَمَآ أَدْرَىٰكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ (٢) لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍۢ (٣)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Indeed, We sent the Qur'an down during the Night of Decree.
And what can make you know what is the Night of Decree?
The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Say the noon clearly before the hamza
The qaf has sukoon, so it bounces
The noon is hidden with a light hum

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 97:1-3 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which ayah says the Night of Decree is better than a thousand months?
check.why: 97:3 says it is better than a thousand months. 97:1 says the Qur'an was sent down on it; 97:2 asks what will make you know it.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Qadr 97:1-3 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 97:1-3 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 97:1-3. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.q: Laylat al-Qadr means ...
practice.a: the Night of Decree

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 97:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, write what 'Laylat al-Qadr' means in your own words.
independent.a: The Night of Decree: the night the Qur'an was first sent down, better than a thousand months.

independent.q: Find the word in 97:1 with a qalqalah letter. Why does it bounce?
independent.a: ٱلْقَدْرِ: the qaf (ق) has a sukoon, so it bounces.

exit.q: Al-Qadr 97:3: «لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: خَيْرٌۭ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Why might one special night be better than a thousand months?
exit.a: Allah chose it: the Qur'an was first sent down on it, and good deeds on it are worth more than a thousand months (97:3).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Qadr 97:1-3 to a parent three times a day and revise Al-Fatihah and Surahs 114 to 98 (today's rota surah); tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: At-Tin and the noon sakinah rules
lessons.title: Noon sakinah and tanween: the four rules and izhar
lessons.bigQuestion: If you whisper 'min ahli' and then 'min-n-n ahli', which sounds clearer? Why do you think clear matters in the Qur'an?
objectives: To understand how to spot noon sakinah and tanween and say the noon clearly (izhar) before the six throat letters
successCriteria: All: point to a noon sakinah and a tanween in an ayah
Most: name the six throat letters of izhar
Some: read three izhar examples clearly, with no humming
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: care in reciting Allah's words exactly as they were taught

keywords.def: a noon with a sukoon on it: نْ
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon
saying the noon clearly, with no extra humming
the throat, where the six izhar letters come from

hook.text: If you whisper 'min ahli' and then 'min-n-n ahli', which sounds clearer? Why do you think clear matters in the Qur'an?
hook.a: Clear speech keeps the meaning right. Before the throat letters the noon is said clearly: that is izhar.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Tajweed rules help us recite the way the Prophet ﷺ was taught.

starter.q: What does sukoon (ْ) do to a letter?
starter.a: It has no vowel: the letter stops
options: It has no vowel: the letter stops

starter.q: Which shows tanween?
Al-Qadr 97:1: «إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ...» Which word comes next?

teach.heading: Two kinds of 'n' sound
bullets: Both follow the same four rules
The next letter decides the rule
teach.note: Bismillah. Write نْ and ـٌ ـً ـٍ on the board. Tanween only comes at the end of a word; noon sakinah can be in the middle or at the end.

keywords.def: changing the noon into a hidden meem before baa
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts

hook.text: Try saying 'n' and then 'b' quickly: 'min ba'd'. What do your lips want to do?

islamicLink.text: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'The one who is skilled in the Qur'an will be with the noble and righteous scribes (angels), and the one who recites it with difficulty, stumbling, has two rewards' (Bukhari and Muslim). Every effort counts.

starter.q: «عِيشَةٍۢ رَّاضِيَةٍۢ» is ...

teach.heading: Iqlab: one letter, ب
bullets: Noon or tanween becomes a meem sound
Lips close gently, hum two counts
teach.note: Bismillah. Iqlab means turning over or changing. The noon is not said; a hidden meem with ghunnah takes its place, then the baa.

teach.heading: The small meem sign
teach.note: In the Madinah mushaf a small meem (ۢ) sits over the noon or by the tanween. Show it on screen.

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Some pupils press the lips hard (a full meem). Keep it light: lips just touch.

misconception.wrong: min ba'd: a clear noon, or a hard 'mm' pressed shut
misconception.right: mim-ba'd: lips touch lightly, two-count hum, then baa

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: hidden meem
teach.note: Pupils unmute in turn. Ask them to look at their lips on camera: lips touch, hum, then baa.
cycle: Teacher checks: hum and light lips

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.why: Only baa makes iqlab. مِنْ عَلَقٍ is izhar ('ayn); مِّن كُلِّ is ikhfa (kaaf).

practice.q: Read «لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ» (104:4). Find the iqlab and say how to read it.
practice.a: Noon sakinah before baa inside the word: layum-badhanna, lips touching, two-count hum.
practice.model: I do: I see a small meem over the noon in لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ. The next letter is baa. So it is iqlab: I close my lips lightly and hum for two counts: 'layum...badhanna'.

practice.q: Iqlab happens before ...
practice.a: ب

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, find the iqlab in Al-Humazah (104) and Al-Bayyinah 98:4 and draw the small meem sign above each. Today's rota group recites Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 8 to the teacher in turn.
independent.model: The teacher finds the first: in 104:4 the noon in لَيُنۢبَذَنَّ comes before baa, so we mark a small meem.

independent.q: Extend: write the four rules of noon sakinah with one letter for each.
independent.a: Izhar: ء; idgham: م; iqlab: ب; ikhfa: (week 5) for example ك.

independent.q: Stretch: why do you think the noon turns into meem before baa?
independent.a: Meem and baa are both made with the lips, so a meem sound flows easily into the baa.

exit.q: The small meem (ۢ) in the mushaf tells us ...
exit.a: it is iqlab

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Try saying 'n' and then 'b' quickly: 'min ba'd'. What do your lips want to do?
exit.a: They close, so the noon turns into a meem sound: iqlab. The mushaf shows a small meem (ۢ) to tell us.

lessons.smsc: Moral: we never stop anyone from doing good; we help others to pray

hook.text: Have you ever seen someone stop another person from doing something good? What should we do?
hook.a: Al-'Alaq 96:9 to 12 warns about someone who stops a servant of Allah from praying; we help others to do good.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays?' (Al-'Alaq 96:9 to 10). These ayat teach us that stopping someone from salah is a serious wrong, and that guidance and taqwa are what matter (96:11 to 12).

Which word means 'the return'?

Follow each word with your finger

lessons.title: Ikhfa and the noon sakinah check
lessons.bigQuestion: Is hiding always bad? When the Qur'an 'hides' a noon, why might that make the recitation more beautiful?
objectives: To understand how noon sakinah and tanween are hidden with ghunnah before the fifteen ikhfa letters, and to use all four rules
successCriteria: All: read three ikhfa examples with a light hum
Most: name the rule for any noon sakinah from its next letter
Some: score 8 out of 10 or more on the four-rules check
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: joy at finishing a set of rules; thanking Allah for progress

keywords.def: hiding the noon with a light humming sound
a humming sound from the nose, held for two counts
a noon with a sukoon on it: نْ
a double vowel at the end of a word that sounds like an extra noon

hook.text: Is hiding always bad? When the Qur'an 'hides' a noon, why might that make the recitation more beautiful?
hook.a: Ikhfa is a gentle, half-hidden noon with a hum: smoother than a clear noon, lighter than full merging.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation (tartil)' (Al-Muzzammil 73:4). Today we finish the four rules Allah's Messenger ﷺ recited with.

starter.q: Iqlab happens before ...
«يَكُن لَّهُۥ» is ...
Recite Al-'Alaq 96:9 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Ikhfa: the hidden noon
teach.note: Bismillah. Ikhfa means hiding. The tongue does not press for the noon; we hum through the nose while getting ready for the next letter.

teach.heading: The fifteen letters
teach.note: Count them together: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك. If it is not izhar, idgham or iqlab, it is ikhfa.

teach.heading: All four rules
teach.note: Sort the cards on screen together: which column does each go in? Answers in the notes.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: light hum
teach.note: Pupils unmute in turn for each ikhfa example. Then the noon sakinah check: each pupil reads two words and names the rule.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: «مِّن كُلِّ» (97:4): the next letter is kaaf (ك). Which rule?
check.why: Kaaf is one of the fifteen ikhfa letters. It is not a throat letter (izhar) or in يَرْمَلُونَ (idgham).

practice.q: Read «أَنزَلْنَٰهُ» (97:1): find the noon and name the rule.
practice.a: The noon before zay (ز) is ikhfa: read an-zalnaahu with a light two-count hum.
practice.model: I do: the noon in أَنزَلْنَٰهُ has no vowel. Next letter: ز. Zay is not a throat letter, not in يَرْمَلُونَ, not baa: so ikhfa. I hum lightly as I move to the zay.

practice.q: Which is an ikhfa letter?
practice.a: ك

independent.q: Noon sakinah check (pupil PDF): for ten words from Al-Qadr, Al-'Alaq and Al-Masad, write the rule. Today's rota group recites 96:1 to 12 to the teacher in turn.
independent.a: 1 مِنْ عَلَقٍ izhar; 2 أَنزَلْنَٰهُ ikhfa; 3 مِّن كُلِّ ikhfa; 4 خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْ idgham with ghunnah; 5 مِّنْ أَلْفِ izhar; 6 أَن رَّءَاهُ idgham without ghunnah; 7 إِن كَانَ ikhfa; 8 مِّن مَّسَدٍ idgham with ghunnah; 9 لَهَبٍۢ وَتَبَّ idgham with ghunnah; 10 عَبْدًا إِذَا izhar.
independent.model: The teacher does word 1: مِنْ عَلَقٍ, next letter ع, a throat letter, so izhar.

independent.q: Extend: write the fifteen ikhfa letters from memory.
independent.a: ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك

independent.q: Stretch: explain to the class the difference between ikhfa and idgham with ghunnah.
independent.a: Idgham: the noon disappears into the next letter (shaddah). Ikhfa: the noon is hidden but not merged; no shaddah.

exit.a: ikhfa

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Is hiding always bad? When the Qur'an 'hides' a noon, why might that make the recitation more beautiful?
exit.a: Ikhfa is a gentle, half-hidden noon with a hum: smoother than a clear noon, lighter than full merging.
